en: The Ritual for the Empowerment of the Great Maṇḍala of the Ācārya.

At that time, Vajrapāṇi addressed the Buddha, saying: “World-Honored One! If there are good sons or good daughters who enter this Samaya of the Great King of Maṇḍalas Born from the Treasury of Great Compassion, [what shall be their destiny]?”
"How much of a mass of merit will he obtain?
Having spoken thus, the Buddha addressed Vajrapāṇi, saying:
"Lord of Secrets!..."
From the first generation of the mind of awakening until the attainment of the state of a Tathāgata, the mass of merit possessed by that son or daughter of good family is equal to that mass of merit.
Lord of Mysteries!
You should understand this Dharma-gate in this way:
those sons and daughters of good family are born from the mouth of the Tathāgata; they are the children of the Buddha’s heart.
In whatever place such sons or daughters of good family may dwell, there the Buddha himself performs the work of a Buddha.
Therefore, O Lord of Secrets!
If one wishes to make offerings to the Buddha, one should make offerings to these sons and daughters of good family.
If one wishes to see the Buddha, one should immediately contemplate them as those capable of crushing the armies of Māra and bringing benefit and happiness to all.
Therefore, you who wish to attain the true wisdom of all Tathāgatas should practice this Dharma with a single-minded focus, for it can swiftly bring about the accomplishment of all-knowledge.
The *Saddharmapuṇḍarīka-sūtra* says, "With a pure mind, one believes in and reveres the Buddha";
the *Vimalakīrti-nirdeśa-sūtra* says, "Born from immeasurable merit and wisdom. [The practitioner] should empower five-colored threads and tie them around their left arm.

The mantra is: (1) Oṃ mahā-vajra-kavaca vajri kuru vajra vajra haṃ. Homage to the Great Holy Tathāgata Vairocana of the Vajradhātu; homage to the Tathāgata Akṣobhya of the East; homage to the Tathāgata Ratnasambhava of the South; homage to the Tathāgata Avalokiteśvararāja of the West; homage to the Tathāgata Amoghasiddhi of the North. Homage to Samantabhadra-Vajrasattva and all the Bodhisattvas Mahāsattvas throughout the three periods of time, within the layered net of the ten directions, across the entirety of space and the pervasive Dharma-realm, in lands as numerous as the atoms of dust.
Next, one should mentally recite this secret mantra to protect all disciples.
The secret mantra is:
(2) Oṃ mahā-vajra-kavaca-vajriṇi vajra-hūṃ vajra-phaṭ. Next, empower the unguents and apply them to the palms of the disciples.
The mantra is: “(3) Oṃ vajragandhe khaḥ. When applying the fragrant ointment, one says:
“May you all be fully endowed with the fragrance of the morality, concentration, wisdom, liberation, and the knowledge and vision of liberation of all Tathāgatas.”
Next, empower a white flower and bestow it upon the disciple.
The mantra is: (4) Oṃ vajrapuṣpe oṃ. Then, address them as follows:
"May you all attain the inexhaustible ocean of marks of all Tathāgatas.
Next, empower the incense burner and fumigate the two hands of the disciples.
The mantra is as follows:
(5) Oṃ vajradhūpe hūṃ. He said: "May you all obtain the wondrous color nourished by the inexhaustible great compassion of all Tathāgatas."
Next, empower the lamp and have the disciple gaze at it.
The mantra is: (6) Oṃ hrūḥ lu-ke-ni-sva. Then, address them as follows:
"May you all attain the wisdom of all Tathāgatas, which is equal to the realm of space.

With the empowerment of the mantra of the Radiant Vajra Sword, one should blend the five products of the cow—milk, curd, ghee, dung, and urine—and having clarified and strained them, one should cause [the disciple] to drink them, reciting:
(7) Oṃ vajrodanakta. One should cause them to drink.

Mantra: “(8) Oṃ mahā-juvala hūṃ. Next, empower a tooth-stick (*udumbara*) ten finger-widths long with either the mantra of the Vajra-sword of the profound wisdom of all Buddhas or the *hṛdaya-mantra* (heart-mantra) of the family, which destroys all afflictions (*kleśa*) and secondary afflictions (*upakleśa*). Wash it with scented water, smear it, and fumigate it; wrap flowers around its base and offer one to all the Buddhas, giving the remainder to the practitioner.
Having empowered it with the *Acala-vidyā* and the teeth of one hundred and eight Tathāgatas, he next hands over the tooth-stick (*dantakāṣṭha*).
Having retreated to the place where the precepts are conferred, the candidate chews the small end. He is then asked:
"In whichever direction you cast the tooth-stick, that shall be your direction."
The Sage spoke these verses:
"You have attained incomparable benefit; Your status is equal to that of the Great Self.
All Tathāgatas Instruct all Bodhisattvas thus:"
"I shall embrace you all to accomplish this great task. Tomorrow, you shall be born into the Mahāyāna.

Having said this, he cast [the seed] to examine its signs, instructing them to sit in a squatting posture and chew it while facing east or north; facing outward results in non-accomplishment, while facing inward results in accomplishment.

If one distances oneself from the *kṣapa* for a long time, one accomplishes the East, Above, West, Center, South, and Below; the four directions are mostly of that section. Third, one ties the *sūtra*:

it should be bound with five-colored threads empowered by the five Buddhas upon the arm of *samādhi*. These threads gather and encompass the myriad practices, causing them to abide upon the arm of *samādhi*; as they pass through countless *asaṃkhyeya-kalpas* without being lost or destroyed, it is therefore called the "Vajra Knot."

Next, when traveling at night, cover one's head with red cloth and empower it one hundred and eight times with the mantra and the mantra of Acala; this shall close the gates to all evil realms and enable the accomplishment of the opening of the five pure eyes.
Having bound the *samaya-mudrā*, he orally imparts this secret mantra:

“(9) *Samayas tvaṃ*. He then causes [the disciple] to join the two fingers—the *kaniṣṭhā* and *anāmikā*—upright like a needle and leads him into the gate of the maṇḍala. Three times he imparts this secret word, the *Vajrāṅkuśa-mantra* for leading [the disciple] in:
“(10) *Samaya hūṃ*. He should then say:
"You have now entered the assembly of the Tathāgata’s retinue; I shall now cause you to give birth to vajra-wisdom.
By means of this wisdom, you shall attain the supreme accomplishment of all Tathāgatas, and all worldly and transcendent *siddhi* activities shall be fully accomplished."
Furthermore, you must not explain this ritual matter before anyone who has not yet entered the maṇḍala and received empowerment.
If you do so, you will not only violate your samaya, but will also bring calamity and retribution upon yourself.
The master should firmly bind the wisdom-mudrā of Vajrasattva, place it upon the crown of the disciple’s head, and declare:
“This is the samaya-mudrā of Vajrasattva; if you should ever speak of this to one who has not received initiation, it shall cause your head to split asunder.”
Do not give rise to contempt or arrogance toward me; you should instead conceive deep reverence and faith.
You should regard my person as Vajrasattva, and you must carry out all that I instruct with complete devotion.
"If you do not do so, you will invite calamity upon yourself, perhaps meeting an untimely death or falling into hell after death; therefore, you must be careful.
Desiring to cause Vajrasattva to enter the body and mind of the disciple, the Master then forms the Vajrasattva mudrā and declares:
"This is the samaya of Vajrasattva; may it enter your body and mind to accomplish supreme vajra-wisdom."
Recite this secret mantra:
(11) Oṃ vajravesha aḥ. Next, form the wrathful vajra-fist, hooking the ring and little fingers together, and recite the hundred-syllable secret mantra of the Mahāyāna Samaya.
Having recited this, he pulls apart the upper seal.
By the power and efficacy of these secret words, he is able to cause the disciple to enter the vajra-wisdom and realize sublime insight.

By virtue of this wisdom, one is able to fully attain the knowledge of the various mental states of all sentient beings; one can understand the three types of worldly activities, stabilize the bodhicitta, extinguish all suffering and affliction, and become free from all fears. No evil whatsoever can cause harm, all Tathāgatas provide their collective empowerment, and all siddhis manifest before one. All unprecedented, peaceful, and sublime matters are attained spontaneously without being sought.
“You should consider yourself deeply fortunate; I shall now briefly explain for you the preeminent qualities of merit:

through these dharmas, you shall fully attain all the doors of liberation, doors of supernormal powers, doors of samādhi, doors of dhāraṇī, doors of the pāramitās, the ten powers, the fearlessnesses, the unique buddha-qualities, and so forth. Furthermore, the profound meanings of hundreds of thousands of sūtras that you have never before seen or heard will naturally become understood.”
"You shall, before long, personally realize the true wisdom of all Buddhas; how much more so the other, inferior siddhis?
Having spoken these words, one should next ask:
"What kind of vision have you seen? Below this, there are the mantras for destroying sins and so forth—mark it accordingly."
Having successively crushed all sins, one further visualizes that the bodies and minds of those beings are purified by the light of all Buddhas.
From the four directions, Akṣobhya and the others, and from above, Mahāvairocana Tathāgata and the others, all emit pure light;
from below, one visualizes the Vajrasattva emitting the syllable HŪṂ, which radiates wrathful light to crush [the defilements].
When performing this rite, one will certainly cause them to perceive auspicious signs; it should be known that their karmic obstructions are thereby extinguished.
If their offenses are extremely grave such that they do not see favorable signs, the master should recite the true gāthās for them to bring about their awakening.
The verse says:
"Samantabhadra’s true body pervades all; he is the sovereign king of the world.
Without beginning or end, without birth or cessation, his nature and characteristics are eternally abiding, equal to space."
The minds of all sentient beings are the firm Bodhi, hence they are called *sattva*;
when the mind abides unmoving in *samādhi*, its diligent determination is called *vajra*.

I now speak these words of truth; I pray only that the World-Honored One, upholding his original vow, for the sake of the *siddhi* of all sentient beings, will out of compassion and pity grant his empowerment.
Having spoken these words, he again formed the Vajra-entrance mudrā and recited the secret mantra of the letter *Aṃ* one hundred and eight times.

He then formed the Vajra-bond (*vajrabandha*), pressing the tips of the wisdom fingers (*prajñā-aṅguli*) against the base joints of the dharma fingers (*dharma-aṅguli*), while slightly bending the tips of the effort fingers (*vīrya-aṅguli*) so that they touch one another. This is it.

Having performed the ritual procedure in this manner, if no auspicious signs (*lakṣaṇa*) are perceived, one should merely lead the candidate in and administer the *samaya*, but should not confer the empowerment (*abhiṣeka*).
Next, one should administer the following secret mantra (*mantra*) three times:
*Oṃ vajra-samaya-mahā-krodha hūṃ phaṭ* (Recite this). Then recite the *Vajrasattva-samaya-mantra*: *Oṃ vajra-samaya-satvo aho hi hi hi hi hūṃ* (Join this to the *Vajrasattva-samaya-mantra*).

(12) Having recited “Oṃ pratīccha vajra hūṃ,” have them cast the flower. Wherever the flower lands, one shall receive the secret mantra of the Honored One of that family and will swiftly attain accomplishment:

if the flower falls upon the face of the Buddha or upon the Honored Ones such as Locanā, one accomplishes the Heart Mantra; if it falls within the center of the Buddha’s body, one accomplishes the Mantra of the Mind; if it falls on the lower part of the Buddha’s body, one accomplishes the Mantra of the Messenger.
Next, recite this mantra three times and release the *samaya* mudrā bound by the disciple upon their heart.
The mantra is: "May Vajrasattva abide eternally and firmly; may he empower my mind and grant me all *siddhis*. This is the Vajra-liberation mantra:
(13) Oṃ tiṣṭha vajra-nirmita bhava śāstu-mate bhava hṛdaye me ātiṣṭha sarva-siddhi-samaye praveśaya hūṃ ha ha ha ha hoḥ. Reciting this mantra, remove the cloth that covers the eyes.
The secret mantra says:
"The flower you have cast is placed upon your crown; the Sattva accepts it, and you shall swiftly attain all siddhis. (14) Oṃ vajrasattvasādhayantiye krodha ṭaṅkadhāra.
Dhāraya bhaṅga-ghātaya ti sarvavratidhara vajracakra ānuttaraṇa he vajrapāṇe.

"Vajrasattva himself has personally and exclusively opened for you the five eyes, the unsurpassed Vajra-eye. Next, he calls the disciple's name and shows him all the ritual implements and characteristics of the various families within the maṇḍala.
By virtue of this dharma, one is embraced and protected by all Tathāgatas, and Vajrasattva dwells eternally within one’s heart.

Whatever one seeks, up to and including the body of a Vajradhara, shall be obtained without exception; one will gradually enter into the dharmic nature of the essence of all Tathāgatas. If one beholds this maṇḍala, the manifold karmic offenses accumulated over immeasurable koṭis of kalpas will be entirely extinguished thereby.

Next, one should lead the recipient of the consecration to step upon the flower at the gate with the left foot and the center of the flower with the right foot, entering the gate in the direction of the Lord of Devas. There, they sit upon the flower pedestal and are honored with various flowers, unguents, incense, lamps, banners, canopies, and sublime music.
If one cannot discern [the specific details], one should perform them according to one's capacity.
The reason for this is that such a person sits upon the seat of the Buddha.
Furthermore, by means of various hymns and songs of praise, one causes them to give rise to a profound sense of joy.
He spoke this verse:
"When the Buddhas descend from Tuṣita to be born, Indra, Brahmā, nāgas, and spirits attend and protect them;
May you now obtain all such various, supreme, wondrous, and auspicious matters."
Born in the palace of the Śākyas in Kapilavastu, The dragon kings showered him with nectar-water;
May the auspicious offerings of all the devas Grant you consecration in like manner.
Upon the vajra seat for the sake of all sentient beings, At the final watch of night, you subdue Māra and attain perfect enlightenment;
Manifesting all manner of rare and auspicious events— May you fully accomplish this very seat.
In the groves and rivers of Vārāṇasī, you opened the wondrous Dharma for the five sages;
having accomplished immeasurable auspicious deeds, may you now attain them all.
The ocean of the great compassion and skillful means of all Buddhas universally benefits the ocean of sentient beings throughout the Dharma-realm;
without weariness until the end of the future, you shall attain the four types of unimpeded wisdom.
If there are further verses of praise, one may compose them as desired to inspire superior resolve and give rise to beneficial joy.
Next, one should confer the empowerment upon them.
First, visualize the syllable *Aṃ* at the crown of the disciple’s head, emitting great flames of light, blazing and resplendent.
Then, visualize a moon disc within the disciple’s heart; within that moon disc is an eight-petaled lotus, and upon its center is also the syllable *Āḥ*.
If one obtains the Vajra family, one should visualize a five-pronged vajra within the syllable *Aṃ*; the other families may be understood accordingly.
If one obtains [a deity] such as Vajrapadma, one should cause each to form the mudrā of their respective family.
Place it upon the crown of the head and recite the mantra of the respective family seven times to perform the consecration (*abhiṣeka*).
The mantras for the Vajra Family consecrations are as follows:

(15) Oṃ vajrasattva viśodhaya hūṃ | Oṃ vajraratna viśodhaya traṭ | Oṃ vajradharma viśodhaya hrīḥ | Oṃ vajrakarma viśodhaya aḥ || Visualize the syllable *laḥ* on their foreheads, the color of pure gold.
Above each of the two eyes is the syllable *ra*, its color like fire and topped with blazing flames;
between the two feet, one should visualize various colors forming the mark of a Dharma wheel, adorned with eight spokes.
Next, recite the Heart Mantra of Vajrasattva and empower the unguent to smear upon the disciple’s chest.
The reason for performing this rite of empowerment is to cause the disciple to become like Vajrasattva.
Next, form the seal of Vairocana and recite the root mantra. Place the mudrā upon the [practitioner’s] heart, then on the forehead, then at the throat, and finally upon the crown of the head.

One should then clearly visualize the secret, supreme, and exalted crowns of all Tathāgatas being placed upon that head. Then, form the four types of garland seals as described above, binding them to the forehead according to the specific ritual methods of each respective family.
If one performs the *ācārya-abhiṣeka*, one should employ all five vases in succession according to the aforementioned method; having then bound four types of garlands in sequence upon the forehead.

Next, the master, holding a five-pronged vajra with its feathers, places it in the disciple’s two hands. He should then encourage, guide, and comfort him through various skillful means and words, reciting this verse:
“The ritual for the Vajra-Abhiṣeka of all Buddhas— You have already received this consecration according to the Dharma.
In order to realize the essential nature of the Tathāgata, You should now accept this vajra.”
Having recited this verse, the mantra is as follows:
(16) Oṃ vajrabhūti vicitrami tiṣṭha vajrasamayas tvaṃ. Then, he should take up the vajra again.
If one belongs to the Ratna family, one should further visualize a jewel atop the vajra; the other families should follow this example.
When reciting the aforementioned mantra, the word "vajra" in the first phrase should be changed to "jewel," and the other families should conform to this accordingly.
Next, prefix the disciple’s original name with the word *vajra* and address them by that name.
One should recite this mantra:

(17) Oṃ vajrasattva viśodhaya vajrānma āviśa hī vajrānma. Furthermore, one should offer incense, flowers, and various ritual implements to the one who has received the consecration. The master, holding a small *vajra*, should wipe their two eyes as in the rite for treating the eyes and address them thus:
“Good son! Just as a physician-king of the world can remove the cataracts of the eyes,
so too do the Buddhas, the Tathāgatas, today open the cataract of ignorance for you, in order to enable you to attain the adamantine eye of wisdom and perceive the true reality of all phenomena.”
Next, he again held up a mirror and had him look into it, in order to reveal that the nature and characteristics of all phenomena are empty and quiescent.
He spoke a verse, saying:
“The nature of all phenomena Is such that neither defilement nor purity can be found.”
Neither real nor unreal, all manifest from causes and conditions.
You should know that all phenomena have no basis in their own nature;
you are now a true son of the Buddha, bringing vast benefit to all sentient beings.
The teacher should conceive a sense of reverence toward the disciple, for this person is capable of succeeding to the lineage of all Buddhas.
The teacher should present him with a conch shell and address him thus:

"From this day forward, you shall turn the Wheel of Dharma of all Buddhas; you shall blow the unsurpassed conch of the Dharma, so that the sound of the Great Dharma pervades all places. You must not give rise to doubt or fear regarding this Dharma."
Regarding the principles of practice for the ultimate purity of all secret mantras, you should extensively and skillfully reveal them to sentient beings.
Son of good family, listen attentively:
if one can practice in this manner, all Tathāgatas will know that you are able to repay the Buddha’s kindness.
"Therefore, at all times and in all places, you shall be protected by all Vajradharas, who will bring you peace and happiness.
Next, one should lead them forward to the great mandala, explain the samaya to make it firm, and address them, saying:
"O son of noble family!"
You should steadfastly uphold the True Dharma; even if you encounter oppression, suffering, or even the loss of life, you must not abandon the cultivation of the bodhicitta.
You should not be stingy regarding those who seek the Dharma or with material wealth, nor should you perform even the slightest act that is unbeneficial to sentient beings.
This is the supreme meaning of the words, the sphere of the noble ones; I have now fully explained it for you, and you should practice accordingly in accordance with what has been taught.
The disciple should rejoice and prostrate with palms joined.
Furthermore, [the master] takes a five-pronged vajra and hands it to him, saying:
"This is the essential nature of all Buddhas, held in the hand of Vajrasattva; you should firmly protect the prohibitive precepts and always uphold it."
Once the disciple has received [the initiation], the teacher should cause him to recite this essential vow of the secret mantra (*guhyamantra*).
The mantra is as follows:

(18) Oṃ sarvatathāgatasiddhivajrasamayatistha eṣa tvāṃ dhārayāmi vajrasattva hī hī hī hī hūṃ. Having performed the ritual in this manner, the master should instruct the disciple in all the secret samaya-wisdom of the maṇḍala.
If a disciple should fall away from the samaya, the master should restrain them so as not to let it be destroyed.
The disciple should show reverence and respect toward the master, not seeing his faults, and should harbor no resentment toward their fellow students.
One should address them, saying:
"You should always give rise to compassion and pity for all sentient beings, showing them mercy and instruction; do not harbor feelings of weariness or detachment.
Then, one should speak these verses:
"The most grievous sins within the three realms / Do not exceed weary detachment;
/ Within the sphere of desire, / Do not give rise to a mind of weary detachment.
Next, wishing to cause the disciple to maintain joy with firm resolve, he further spoke this verse:
"These samayas have been taught to you by all the Buddhas;
maintain them well and guard them with care, as if protecting your own life.
Having received the teacher's instruction, the disciple prostrates at the teacher's feet and says:
“As you have instructed, I vow to practice accordingly.
He then makes this dedication and aspiration:
“I, disciple [Name] and others, having from the very beginning listened to the True Dharma before this Great Mandala of the Matrix of Great Compassion, have given rise to pure faith.”

I prostrate and invite the assembly of holy ones from the ocean-like gathering; I take refuge in the Triple Gem, repent and eliminate the defilements of my transgressions, and receive the pure precepts of the Buddha.
Having cast this flower with a karmic affinity, I am blessed by the compassionate protection of the Sages and have already attained the title and office of a consecrated Vajra-holder.

Following the stages of the noble ones—whose boundless merits are as incalculable as the sands of the Ganges—I dedicate them all to the sentient beings of the Dharma-realm, wishing that they may all be freed from suffering and attain peaceful happiness; that they may abandon the false and return to the correct path, resolve to attain Bodhicitta, practice the Bodhisattva path without ever regressing, and attain Buddhahood simultaneously in a future age.
Eliminating the three karmas of ignorance and delusion, one immediately attains the moon-disc of the *sattva* mind;
firmly non-retrogressive in the three secret practices, oneself and others will fully accomplish *siddhi*.

In the late autumn of the Gengshen year, the twelfth year of the Kōan era, in order to complete the printing of the Fūzan edition which had remained unfinished, I collated it against the transmitted original and several other variant manuscripts, and then punctuated it.
In the fifth month of the year Xinyou of the Xiange era,
the śramaṇa Zhenchang of Mount Yaoshu in Henan further collated and corrected this [text] using a copy from Zhiji Monastery in the capital.
The postscript states:

"This one fascicle of the *Ācārya-abhiṣeka-vidhi* contains Sanskrit phrases and meanings not found in previous editions; now, following the oral instructions of my teacher, I have privately added them here. However, its phrasing and meanings are entirely based upon the commentary to the *Lüchù jīng* (Simplified Extract of the Sūtra) in four fascicles."
In the course of transcribing it, I have read through several passages; the literary garden is overgrown with weeds and the paths of meaning are impassable.
Upon closer examination, I find that the descriptions of the phenomena are frequently mangled and missing; thus, I have ventured to offer a humble glimpse into a single portion of this work.
In the *Fushi Shari* (Notes on the Negation of Consciousness), it is recorded:

"The third day of the ninth month in the third year of the Genroku era, the Gengwu year. The disciple of the Nanto school, Keikō, of the Inner Province, aged twenty-five, records his aspirations. [He notes:

"Thus, while these Sanskrit phrases and meanings were added later, they have been omitted over the long course of transcription; or perhaps there are cases where only the Sanskrit exists and the Chinese translation has been lost. I await a time to re-collate a superior manuscript."
